“Did the show go well?”

zh: “还行吧，老样子，挺热闹的。”
月牙儿一边漫不经心的答着，一边摆弄那架天文望远镜。她显然是第一次碰这种东西，低着头研究了半天，动作里带着一点新鲜，也带着一点不服气。生锈的望远镜的金属支架轻轻作响，目镜缓缓抬高，对准夜空里那轮异常明亮的月亮。
en: “It was fine. Same as usual. Pretty lively.”

Mahina answered absently while fiddling with the astronomical telescope. It was clearly her first time handling such a thing. She lowered her head and studied it for a long while, her movements carrying both curiosity and a trace of stubbornness. The rusty metal stand creaked softly as the eyepiece slowly rose, aiming toward the unusually bright moon in the night sky.

zh: 希扬翻起盖在脸上的书的一角，偏头看了她一眼，开口道：
“先别急着从目镜里看。”
月牙儿停了停，朝他那边望过去。
希扬抬手朝望远镜侧边点了点。
“看到旁边那个红点寻星镜没有？先拿手柄慢慢调，让里面的红点对准你想看的地方，再去调主镜，不然你很难定位。”
en: Suvan lifted one corner of the book covering his face, turned his head to glance at her, and said:
“Don’t look through the main eyepiece yet.”
Mahina paused and looked over at him.
Suvan raised a hand and pointed toward the side of the telescope.

“See that little red-dot finder on the side? Move it slowly with the controller first. Put the red dot on whatever you want to look at, then adjust the main scope. Otherwise it’s hard to find anything.”

zh: 月牙儿顺着他说的低头找了找，果然在侧边看见一个很小的瞄准镜。她照着他的意思开始尝试，微微眯起眼，指尖按着操控器，一点一点移动方向。外面的月亮亮得惊人，红点在黑暗里轻轻挪动了很久，才终于慢慢落到月面正中。
她俯下身，把眼睛凑近目镜，下一秒，便低低地“哇”了一声。
en: Mahina followed his instructions and lowered her head to search. Sure enough, she found a tiny sight on the side. She began trying it his way, narrowing one eye slightly, her fingertips pressing the controller as she moved it bit by bit. The moon outside was startlingly bright. The red dot drifted through the dark for a long while before finally settling at the center of the lunar surface.
She bent down and brought her eye close to the eyepiece. The next second, she let out a soft “wow.”

zh: 月亮一下子近得惊人，冷白，安静，巨大的轮廓在黑暗的夜空中显得异常锋利。表面粗粝的纹理、环形山的阴影、深邃的月海，全都分明地浮在那里，安静得近乎庄严，像一张苍白又古老的脸。
月牙儿就这样对着目镜看了很久，才轻声问道：
“它是不是一直只拿这一面对着我们？”
希扬的声音从身后传来，平静而简短：
“对。因为月亮的公转周期和自转周期是一样的，它绕着地球转一圈，自己也刚好转完一圈，所以朝着我们的，永远都是这一面。”
月牙儿安静地听着，像是在脑子里把这件事转了一遍，随后又问：
“这是巧合吗？”
“也不能算巧合。” 希扬说， “关于这件事，有两种解释，看你更喜欢哪一种。”
月牙儿把眼睛从目镜前稍稍挪开一点。
“哪两种？”
en: The moon was suddenly astonishingly close: cold white, silent, its huge outline unnaturally sharp against the dark sky. The rough texture of its surface, the shadows of craters, the deep lunar maria all floated there in clear detail, so quiet it was almost solemn, like a pale and ancient face.
Mahina looked through the eyepiece for a long time before asking softly:
“Does it always show us only this side?”
Suvan’s voice came from behind her, calm and brief:
“Yes. Because the Moon’s orbital period and rotation period are the same. It circles Earth once, and in that same time it turns once on its own axis. So the side facing us is always the same side.”
Mahina listened quietly, as if turning the fact over in her mind. Then she asked:
“Is that a coincidence?”
“Not exactly,”  Suvan said.  “There are two explanations. It depends which one you prefer.”
Mahina moved her eye slightly away from the eyepiece.
“What are they?”

zh: “第一种，” 他把手里的笔在桌上转了一圈，慢慢说道，
“月亮刚形成的时候，公转和自转并不是同步的。但在很漫长的时间里，地球对它施加潮汐力，慢慢消耗掉了它自转的差异，最后就把它锁住了。我们现在把这种状态叫潮汐锁定。”
月牙儿点了点头，像是听明白了，顺势又问了一句：
“那另一种呢？”
希扬停了一下，才淡淡道：
“第二种就简单多了。” 希扬的目光落到了她那把白色的贝斯上， “因为月亮不想让别人看见她的另一面。”
月牙儿一愣，很快就明白了话里的弦外之音。
她没有把这句话接下去，只重新对着那轮月亮看了一会儿，过了很久才轻声道：
“原来亲眼这样看月亮，是这种感觉。我以前只在书上和屏幕上见过它，总觉得它只是远远挂在天上的一小块白。现在才发现，它比我想象里更大，也更亮。”
en: “The first,”  he said slowly, twirling the pen in his hand once on the desk,

“is that when the Moon first formed, its orbit and rotation were not synchronized. But over a very long time, Earth exerted tidal forces on it, gradually wearing away the difference in its rotation, until it was finally locked. We call that state tidal locking.”
Mahina nodded, as if she understood, and naturally asked another question:
“And the other one?”
Suvan paused before saying lightly:
“The second is much simpler.”  Suvan’s gaze fell on her white bass.  “Because the Moon doesn’t want anyone to see her other side.”
Mahina froze for a moment, then quickly understood the meaning beneath his words.
She did not answer. She only looked at the moon again for a while. After a long time, she said softly:

“So this is what it feels like to see the moon with your own eyes. I had only seen it in books and on screens before. I always thought it was just a small white patch hanging far away in the sky. Now I realize it is larger than I imagined, and brighter too.”

zh: 她顿了顿，又很轻地补了一句：
“可这些光，也不是它自己的吧，是太阳的光。”
希扬轻轻点了点头。
“那太阳和月亮之间，隔了多远？” 月牙儿像是在想着什么，忽然又问。
希扬坐在那张旧椅子里，神情依旧平静，只是那平静里，像忽然落进了一层更深的东西。
过了片刻，他才低声道：
“光要走八分半。”
“八分半？听起来并不远。”
希扬没有接话。
那一瞬间，月牙儿觉得他像是想说什么，却最终还是没有说出口。她也没有追问，只把目光重新落回月亮上。夜风从窗缝里慢慢漏进来，吹得那道淡蓝色的布帘轻轻动了一下。
安静了一会儿，她忽然又问：
“为什么一说到距离，总要拿光来算？”
“因为光速，是这个宇宙最底层的法则。” 他说， “一切有序信息的极限速度，都是光速。只要你还在这个法则之内，就没有任何东西能真正越过它，到达光锥之外。”
“光锥之外？”
月牙儿听到“光锥之外”这个词，整个人都警觉起来。
“张良那天说，我们在光锥之外。” 她看着他， “这到底是什么意思？什么叫光锥？光锥之外又是什么地方？”
en: She paused, then added in an even lighter voice:
“But this light isn’t really its own, is it? It’s sunlight.”
Suvan nodded gently.
“Then how far is the Sun from the Moon?”  Mahina suddenly asked, as if thinking of something.
Suvan sat in the old chair, his expression still calm, though something deeper seemed to settle inside that calm.
After a moment, he said in a low voice:
“Light takes eight and a half minutes.”
“Eight and a half minutes? That doesn’t sound very far.”
Suvan did not answer.

In that instant, Mahina felt as if he wanted to say something, but in the end he did not. She did not press him either. She only lowered her gaze back to the moon. The night wind leaked slowly through the gap in the window, stirring the pale blue curtain ever so slightly.
After a while of silence, she suddenly asked again:
“Why do people always use light to measure distance?”

“Because the speed of light is one of the most fundamental laws of this universe,”  he said.  “The speed of light is the limit for all ordered information. As long as you remain inside that law, nothing can truly cross it and arrive beyond the light cone.”
“Beyond the Light Cone?”
When Mahina heard the phrase “beyond the light cone,” her whole body grew alert.
“Zhang Liang said that day that we were beyond the light cone.”  She looked at him.  “What does that mean? What is a light cone? What kind of place is beyond it?”

zh: “来，我给你解释。”
希扬已经站起身，拿起桌上的笔，走到落地窗前，抬手在玻璃上画了一条横线，又画了一条竖线。笔尖划过玻璃，发出很轻的摩擦声。
en: “Come here. I’ll explain.”

Suvan had already stood up. He picked up the pen from the desk, walked to the floor-to-ceiling window, and drew a horizontal line on the glass, then a vertical one. The pen tip scraped lightly across the surface.

zh: 月牙儿不知从哪儿摸出一副圆框眼镜戴上，坐上高脚凳，一本正经地抬头望着他：
“那希扬老师，开始你的物理课吧。”
希扬被她调侃得有点不知所措，只能回头硬着头皮继续在玻璃上画那两条轴线。
“这条横轴，代表时间。往右是未来，往左是过去。原点——就是现在。”
en: From somewhere, Mahina produced a pair of round-framed glasses and put them on. Sitting on the high stool, she looked up at him with mock seriousness:
“Then, Teacher Suvan, please begin your physics lesson.”
Suvan was flustered enough by her teasing that he could only turn back and continue drawing the two axes on the glass.
“This horizontal axis represents time. To the right is the future, to the left is the past. The origin is now.”

zh: 月牙儿扶了扶眼镜，认真地点头道：
“明白。现在，原点。”
“竖轴和另一个你现在看不见的轴，一起构成空间，也就是距离。这个坐标系，就是时空坐标。”
“好。” 月牙儿说， “时空坐标。”
en: Mahina adjusted her glasses and nodded seriously.
“Understood. Now. The origin.”
“The vertical axis, together with another axis you cannot see right now, forms space, or distance. This coordinate system is a spacetime coordinate system.”
“Good,”  Mahina said.  “Spacetime coordinates.”

zh: “假设你出生的时空位置是原点。” 希扬继续往右，在横轴上取了一个点， “而这里，是时间轴上的一百年后，我们把它叫作A点。然后以这个A点为圆心，在空间平面上画一个半径为一百光年的圆。这个圆，就是你在一百年后理论上能抵达的边界。”
月牙儿很快听明白了。
“因为最快也不能超过光速，所以如果是一百年后，理论上最远也只能到一百光年的地方。”
“对。” 希扬说， “再把这个圆和原点连起来，你看它像什么？”
en: “Suppose the spacetime position where you were born is the origin.”  Suvan moved to the right and marked a point on the time axis.  “And here is one hundred years later on the time axis. We’ll call it point A. Then, using point A as the center, draw a circle in the spatial plane with a radius of one hundred light-years. That circle is the theoretical boundary of where you can reach after one hundred years.”
Mahina understood quickly.
“Because nothing can move faster than light. So after one hundred years, the farthest you could theoretically reach would be one hundred light-years away.”
“Right,”  Suvan said.  “Now connect that circle back to the origin. What does it look like?”

zh: 月牙儿眯着眼看了一会儿。
“一个圆锥体。”
“对。” 希扬说， “这就是属于你的光锥。关于你的一切信息，都只能存在在这个范围之内。因为一切有序信息都不可能超过光速，所以它们永远不可能突破这个光锥之壁。你的存在、你的影响，你能到达的地方，你能让别人知道的事——都被关在这个范围里。对光锥之外的任何一个点来说，关于你的信息都到不了那里，所以从它的角度看，你是不存在的。”
en: Mahina narrowed her eyes and looked for a while.
“A cone.”

“Right,”  Suvan said.  “This is your light cone. All information about you can only exist within this range. Because ordered information can never exceed the speed of light, it can never break through the wall of this cone. Your existence, your influence, the places you can reach, the things you can make others know, all of it is confined within this range. For any point outside the light cone, information about you can never arrive. So from its perspective, you do not exist.”

zh: 月牙儿站起身，伸出手前探，仿佛想去触摸那看不见的光锥之壁。
“一个囚笼。” 她轻声道。
希扬没有出声。
她盯着自己轻轻舞动着的手指，仿佛看到命运从指缝间流过，刺痛，而又微凉。
“一个锥形的囚笼，把我们的一生都关在里面了。我们终其一生，永远都到不了它外面。”
en: Mahina stood up and reached forward, as if trying to touch the invisible wall of the light cone.
“A prison,”  she said softly.
Suvan said nothing.
She stared at her own gently moving fingers, as if seeing fate flowing between them, sharp and faintly cold.
“A cone-shaped prison, locking our entire lives inside it. No matter how long we live, we can never reach the outside.”

zh: 落地窗外，月亮的冷光落在玻璃上，那些刚写上去的线条和字迹被月光映得微微发亮，影子斜斜投下来，落在两个人身上，像某种无声覆盖下来的秩序。
过了一会儿，她像是忽然抓住了什么，抬头问他：
“可你刚才说的是，有序信息的极限速度是光速。那是不是意味着，还有一种叫无序信息的东西，可以突破光速？”
希扬终于笑了笑。果然，以她的敏锐，很快就能抓到这条线。
“对。” 他说， “无序信息。”
月牙儿盯着他，眼睛里的光慢慢亮起来。
en: Outside the floor-to-ceiling window, the moon’s cold light fell on the glass. The lines and words freshly written there glimmered faintly in the moonlight, their shadows slanting down over the two of them, like some silent order descending upon them.
After a while, as if suddenly catching hold of something, she looked up and asked him:
“But what you just said was that ordered information has the speed of light as its limit. Does that mean there is another kind of thing called unordered information that can break past light speed?”
Suvan finally smiled. As expected, with her sharpness, she had quickly caught that thread.
“Yes,”  he said.  “Unordered information.”
Mahina stared at him, the light in her eyes slowly brightening.

zh: “你可以先简单理解成这样。假设我手里有两个基本粒子，它们都在做自旋，而且是随机地正旋、反旋，没有固定规律。之后经过某种物理上的绑定，它们会进入一种很特殊的状态——无论相隔多远，它们的变化都会保持瞬时同步，一个怎样旋转，另一个也怎样。”
月牙儿很快接了上去：
“量子纠缠？”
“对。” 希扬点头， “你可以先把它理解成一个最简单的量子纠缠模型。”
en: “You can understand it like this for now. Suppose I have two elementary particles in my hand. Both are spinning, randomly clockwise or counterclockwise, with no fixed pattern. After some kind of physical binding, they enter a very special state. No matter how far apart they are, their changes remain instantaneously synchronized. However one spins, the other spins the same way.”
Mahina caught on quickly:
“Quantum entanglement?”
“Yes.”  Suvan nodded.  “You can understand it first as the simplest model of quantum entanglement.”

zh: 他指向时间轴的左方，像是在指着某个极远的地方。
“现在，我把其中一个粒子送到很远很远的地方。送到一亿光年之外，或者——”
他顿了一下。
en: He pointed toward the left side of the time axis, as if pointing toward some extremely distant place.
“Now I send one of the particles somewhere very, very far away. A hundred million light-years away, or—”
He paused.

zh: “送到两千年前，张良手里。”
月牙儿的目光微微一紧。
“这两个位置，无论是空间上还是时间上，对现在的我们来说，都是光锥之外。
en: “To Zhang Liang’s hand, two thousand years ago.”
Mahina’s gaze tightened slightly.
“Both of these positions, whether in space or in time, are beyond the light cone for us now.

zh: 可如果这两个粒子仍旧保持纠缠，当张良看到他手里的粒子出现正、反、正这样的自旋序列时，他就知道我手里的这一颗，在这一刻也出现了同样的序列。”
“也就是说，” 月牙儿轻声接道， “这条信息传到了两千年前。”
“对。” 希扬说， “这条信息已经越过了光速，到达了光锥之外。”
en: And if these two particles remain entangled, then when Zhang Liang sees the particle in his hand produce a spin sequence of clockwise, counterclockwise, clockwise, he will know that the one in my hand has produced the same sequence at this very moment.”
“In other words,”  Mahina said softly,  “this information reached two thousand years into the past.”
“Yes,”  Suvan said.  “This information has already crossed the speed of light and arrived beyond the light cone.”

zh: 月牙儿皱起了眉：
“我只听说空间上的量子纠缠，时间维度也能纠缠？”
“对。靠纠缠商在数学层面上就可以推算出，时间轴向也存在纠缠。”
“那是不是说，理论上靠量子纠缠，我们能和几光年外的地方进行实时通信，甚至超越时空传递信息？”
希扬摇了摇头。
“不能。”
“为什么？”
“魔鬼就在这里。因为那是一条无序信息。” 希扬说， “它虽然同步，但本身是随机的。你和张良谁都不能决定下一次它是正旋还是反旋。我们只能看见它发生了什么，却无法控制它发生什么。”
月牙儿想了一会儿，又追问：
“如果有一种技术，可以控制它旋转呢？”
en: Mahina frowned.
“I’ve only heard of quantum entanglement across space. Can it happen across time too?”
“Yes. At the mathematical level, the entanglement quotient can be used to infer that entanglement also exists along the time axis.”
“So does that mean, in theory, by relying on quantum entanglement, we could communicate in real time with places several light-years away, even transmit information beyond spacetime?”
Suvan shook his head.
“No.”
“Why?”

“That is the catch. Because it is unordered information,”  Suvan said.  “It is synchronized, but it is random in itself. Neither you nor Zhang Liang can decide whether the next spin will be clockwise or counterclockwise. We can only see what happens. We cannot control what happens.”
Mahina thought for a moment, then asked again:
“What if there were a technology that could control its spin?”

zh: 希扬的声音慢了下来。
“如果你现在伸手去抓住这颗粒子，强行让它按你想要的方式旋转。反、正、反、反——把一个有意义的序列刻进去，借它告诉张良：秦王在后车。”
月牙儿的呼吸轻轻一滞。
“那会怎么样？”
希扬把笔尖停在那两个点之间，轻轻一划，像切断了一根本来看不见的线。
“这条信息就不再是无序的了。而一旦它变成有序信息在光锥之外被观测到，纠缠就会坍缩，这两个粒子之间的联系会立刻断裂，再也无法保持同步。”
“所以，这条信息永远也不可能到张良手里。”
“永远不可能。”
希扬停了停，似乎是故意想留给她一点思考的时间。
“你还记不记得，我们第一次遇见公孙鞅的时候，是在什么时候被传走的？”
月牙儿顺着他的话回想了一会儿，慢慢道：
“是在我叫他商鞅的时候。”
“对。” 希扬说， “因为那个时候，他还不是商鞅，只是公孙鞅。是在后来变法成功、被封到商地之后，他才有了‘商鞅’这个名字。你那一句话，对他来说就是一条来自后世的有序信息。那已经不是普通的交谈了，而是在改动他对自己命运的认知。这样的信息一旦出口，通道就会立刻中断。”
en: Suvan’s voice slowed.

“If you reached out now and seized this particle, forcing it to spin the way you wanted. Counterclockwise, clockwise, counterclockwise, counterclockwise. If you carved a meaningful sequence into it and used it to tell Zhang Liang: the King of Qin is in the rear carriage.”
Mahina’s breath caught softly.
“What would happen?”
Suvan stopped the pen tip between those two points and drew a light stroke, as if cutting an invisible thread.

“Then this information would no longer be unordered. And once it becomes ordered information and is observed beyond the light cone, the entanglement collapses. The connection between the two particles breaks at once, and synchronization can no longer be maintained.”
“So this information can never reach Zhang Liang’s hand.”
“Never.”
Suvan paused, as if deliberately leaving her some time to think.
“Do you remember when we were transported away the first time we met Gongsun Yang?”
Mahina followed his words back through her memory, then slowly said:
“It was when I called him Shang Yang.”

“Right,”  Suvan said.  “Because at that time, he was not Shang Yang yet. He was only Gongsun Yang. Only later, after his reforms succeeded and he was enfeoffed in the land of Shang, did he receive the name ‘Shang Yang.’ That sentence of yours was ordered information from later generations. It was no longer ordinary conversation. It was changing his understanding of his own fate. Once information like that is spoken, the passage immediately cuts off.”

zh: 她只是看着窗上的那些线条，觉得背后慢慢起了一层凉意。像是许多原本散落的碎片，直到这一刻，才终于彼此咬合。
“怪不得那时候我想告诉张良秦王在哪一辆车上，你一下就把我打断了。你不是怕我改变历史，而是——”
突然，月牙儿像是想起了什么，整个人弹了起来。
“怪不得……”
希扬抬起眼。
“什么？”
月牙儿看着他，神情一点点复杂起来。
“怪不得……汉光武帝——”
en: She only looked at the lines on the window, feeling a chill slowly rise along her back. It was as if many scattered fragments had finally locked together at that moment.
“No wonder, when I wanted to tell Zhang Liang which carriage the King of Qin was in, you stopped me at once. You weren’t afraid I would change history. You were—”
Suddenly, as if remembering something, Mahina jolted upright.
“No wonder...”
Suvan raised his eyes.
“What?”
Mahina looked at him, her expression growing complicated little by little.
“No wonder... Emperor Guangwu of Han—”

zh: 希扬愣了一下。
“汉光武帝？”
月牙儿没有立刻解释，只是皱着眉，像是在拼接脑子里一段很旧、很远、原本一直被她当成幻觉的记忆。
“我以前……似乎也遇见过一次。”
希扬的神情少见地凝重了起来。
“什么时候？”
“在西藏。” 月牙儿低声说， “那次我去追盘古云虫的时候。”
她顿了顿，像是在回想那片高原的空气与风。
“那时候我一直以为是高原反应，或者缺氧，以为自己只是做了一个很长很奇怪的梦。”
en: Suvan froze for a moment.
“Emperor Guangwu of Han?”
Mahina did not explain at once. She only frowned, as if piecing together an old and distant memory she had always taken for a hallucination.
“I think... I may have encountered it once before.”
Suvan’s expression turned unusually grave.
“When?”
“In Tibet,”  Mahina said quietly.  “That time I went chasing after the Pangu CloudInsect.”
She paused, as if recalling the air and wind of the plateau.
“At the time, I always thought it was altitude sickness, or lack of oxygen. I thought I had only had a long, strange dream.”

zh: 希扬的手僵在半空，目光紧紧落在她脸上。
“你看见了谁？”
月牙儿沉默了一会儿。
窗外的月亮依旧悬在那里，安静而苍白。她低着头，像是终于从记忆深处摸到了那个名字。
“项羽。”
她说完抬起眼，看向希扬，眼神很深，像还压着另一个没有说出口的名字。
en: Suvan’s hand froze in midair, his gaze fixed tightly on her face.
“Who did you see?”
Mahina was silent for a while.
Outside the window, the moon still hung there, quiet and pale. She lowered her head, as if finally touching that name from the depths of memory.
“Xiang Yu.”
When she finished speaking, she raised her eyes to Suvan. Her gaze was deep, as if it still held another name she had not said aloud.

chapter-5-wuzhui-1.title_zh: 第五章 乌骓 · 一

zh: 月牙儿是被水声唤醒的。
en: The sound of water woke Mahina.

zh: 睁开眼时，头顶是一弯熏黑的竹篷。船身随水波轻轻摇晃，空气里浮着水汽和旧木头的闷味。她低头看自己，一身粗布交领衣裳，袖口磨得起毛。不是她的衣服。
en: When she opened her eyes, a smoke-blackened bamboo canopy arched above her. The boat rocked gently with the current; the damp, close smell of old timber hung in the air. She looked down. She was dressed in a coarse, cross-collared robe, its cuffs worn fuzzy. The clothes were not hers.

zh: 她觉得自己做了一个很长的梦，好像去过很多地方，见过很多人，可真要去想，却又什么都抓不住，只剩一种昏昏沉沉的疲惫压在身上。
en: She felt as though she had dreamed a very long dream—traveled to many places, met many people. Yet whenever she reached for a memory, there was nothing to grasp. Only a leaden weariness remained, pressing down on her body.

zh: 江面浮着晨雾，对岸山影淡得像没干透的墨。没有桥，没有电线，没有任何属于她那个世界的东西。
船头立着一个青年，背对着她，握着一根长竹篙。短褐，肩上打着补丁，裤腿挽到膝盖，小腿沾着干泥，皮肤晒得黝黑。握篙的手指节宽大，结着厚茧，是一双常年同土地和力气打交道的手。他立在船头望着岸上，一动不动，竹篙斜插进江底，船檥在滩边，随时可以离岸。
en: Morning mist drifted over the river. The mountains on the opposite bank were pale as ink not yet dry. No bridge. No power lines. Nothing that belonged to her world.

A young man stood at the bow with his back to her, a long bamboo pole in his hands. His coarse jacket was patched at the shoulder; his trousers were rolled to the knees, his shins caked with dry mud, his skin darkened by the sun. The knuckles around the pole were broad and thick with calluses—the hands of someone long accustomed to earth and hard labor. He stood motionless, watching the shore. The pole slanted into the riverbed, the boat moored against the shoal, ready to cast off at any moment.

zh: 雾越来越浓，一团一团从江面推过来，天光灰白，辨不出时辰。风从岸那边吹来，带着很浓的血腥味，混着烟和马汗的气息。雾的深处隐隐有声音，极远极钝，像几万只马蹄和喊杀被距离磨成一片低低的轰鸣。
青年还在等，目光定定的，像已经等了很久，也不在乎再等多久。
en: The mist thickened, mass upon mass rolling in from the river. The light was ashen; there was no telling the hour. Wind came off the bank, heavy with blood, smoke, and horse sweat. Somewhere deep in the fog, a sound gathered—distant and dull, as though tens of thousands of hooves and battle cries had been ground by distance into a single low thunder.
The young man kept waiting, his gaze fixed. He looked as if he had already waited a very long time, and would not mind waiting longer.

zh: 月牙儿望向乌篷外的江面，起初只有雾。风把雾扯开一道口子的时候，她看见很远的地方立着一个巨大的影子，像山，又不是山。那灰黑的身影几乎和雾融在一起，庞大，沉默，一动不动地立在天地之间，俯瞰着这片江岸，宛若神明。
云虫。
在这个连年代都不知道的地方，她唯一认得的，只有它。它不靠近，也不出声，只是立在那里，像在等着记下即将发生的一切。
en: Mahina looked past the black canopy toward the river. At first there was only fog. Then the wind tore a rent in it, and far away she saw an immense shadow standing there—like a mountain, yet not a mountain. The gray-black form had nearly merged with the mist: vast, silent, unmoving between heaven and earth, looking down upon the riverbank like a god.
CloudInsect.

In a place where she did not even know the century, it was the only thing she recognized. It neither approached nor made a sound. It simply stood there, as though waiting to record everything about to happen.

zh: 不知过了多久，月牙儿才找回自己的声音。
“请问……这是哪里？”
太阳穴一跳一跳地疼。她明明觉得自己经历了很多事，见过很多人，可一件也想不起来，能问出口的，只有这一句。
青年瞥了她一眼，目光又回到岸上。对船里多出来一个人，他似乎并不意外。
“乌江。” 他说， “我们在这儿接一个人。”
en: A long time passed before Mahina found her voice.
“Excuse me… where are we?”
Pain pulsed at her temples. She knew she had lived through many things and met many people, yet she could recall none of them. This was the only question she could manage.
The young man glanced at her, then turned his eyes back to the shore. He did not seem surprised that someone else had appeared in his boat.
“Wujiang.” he said. “We’re here to pick someone up.”

zh: “乌江？接人？”
月牙儿失笑了一声。太离谱了。
“……难不成，是项羽？”
“那……他不会上船的。” 月牙儿不假思索地接了一句。
“我知道。”
他接得更快，平静得像在说今日有雾。
“你怎么知道？” 月牙儿问。
en: “Wujiang? Picking someone up?”
Mahina gave a short, incredulous laugh. It was absurd.
“…Don’t tell me it’s Xiang Yu.”
“Yes.”
“Then… he won’t get on the boat.” The answer escaped Mahina before she had time to think.
“I know.”
His reply came even faster, as calmly as if he were remarking on the fog.
“How do you know?” Mahina asked.

zh: 青年这才回过头来，看了她一眼，微微笑了笑。那笑不是不屑，倒像是早已料到她会这么问。
“姑娘，这世上，又不是只有你一个云中人。”
“……云中人？” 月牙儿皱起眉头。
en: Only then did the young man turn. He looked at her and smiled faintly—not with contempt, but as if he had known all along that she would ask.
“Young lady, you are not the only Cloud Dweller in this world.”
“…Cloud Dweller?” Mahina frowned.

zh: 就在这时，岸上有了动静。
青年脸色一肃，朝她做了个噤声的手势，声音压得极低：
“别出声。他来了。”
en: At that moment, something stirred on the shore.
The young man’s expression sharpened. He raised a finger to his lips and dropped his voice to a whisper:
“Not a sound. He’s here.”

zh: 雾里的芦苇荡先响了一阵，接着，一些身影骑着马，从苇丛中冒了出来。
en: The reeds rustled first. Then riders began to emerge from the fog, one shadow after another pushing through the marsh.

zh: 二十几个士兵，人人带伤，甲胄上满是血污，有人的血还在往下滴，一看就是刚从万军之中杀出来的。为首的是一个异常高大魁梧的身影。断裂的铠甲挂在身上，满脸血污，束发散乱。隔着雾，月牙儿看不清他的容貌，只能望见那道高大而疲惫的轮廓。可那股久经杀伐的压迫感，依旧顺着他手中的战刃穿透雾气，让人心悸。
她瞬间屏住了呼吸。不用任何人告诉她，她已经知道了这个人是谁。
en: There were more than twenty soldiers, every one of them wounded. Their armor was black with blood; some were still bleeding. They looked as though they had just carved their way out of an army. At their head stood an extraordinarily tall, powerfully built man. Broken armor hung from his body. His face was streaked with blood, his bound hair torn loose. Through the fog, Mahina could not make out his features, only the huge, exhausted outline. Yet that oppressive presence, honed through years of bloodshed, still traveled along the blade in his hand, pierced the fog, and made the heart quail.
Her breath stopped. No one had to tell her who he was. She already knew.

zh: 这时，船头的青年高声喊道：
“项王！臣乃乌江亭长，愿渡大王过江。江东虽小，亦有千里之地、数十万百姓，足供大王重整旗鼓！”
“如今江上唯有臣这一条船。请大王速速上船——若汉军追至，便再难渡江了!”
en: The young man at the bow called out:

“King Xiang! I am the Chief of Wujiang Pavilion. Allow me to ferry Your Majesty across the river. Jiangdong may be small, yet it holds a thousand li of land and hundreds of thousands of people—enough for Your Majesty to raise your banners again!”
“Mine is the only boat upon the river. Your Majesty must board at once—if the Han army catches up, there will be no crossing!”

zh: 项羽立在岸边，像是不敢相信这江上竟还有一条渡船。他沉默了很久，才沉沉开口。
“当年，籍与八千江东子弟渡江而西。” 他望着江水，声音不高， “今日，归者无一。”
“纵使江东父兄仍怜我、奉我为王，我有何面目复见之？”
en: Xiang Yu stood at the water’s edge as if he could scarcely believe there was still a ferry on the river. He was silent for a long while before his deep voice came through the mist.
“In years past, I, Ji, crossed westward with eight thousand sons of Jiangdong.” He looked at the river, his voice low. “Today, not one returns.”
“Even if the fathers and elders of Jiangdong still pity me and would make me their king, with what face could I ever meet them again?”

zh: 月牙儿从乌篷里探出半个身子，一直望着岸上。不知是哪里来的胆子，她忽然朝岸上喊了一句：
“项王!他们都是以追随你为荣的，连战死沙场，都引以为荣。他们的父母，怎么会怪罪你呢?”
en: Mahina leaned halfway out from beneath the canopy, watching the shore. She did not know where the courage came from, but suddenly she shouted:
“King Xiang! They were proud to follow you. They were proud even to die beside you in battle. How could their parents blame you?”

zh: 项羽循声望向渡船。看清出声的竟是一个年轻少女，他眼中掠过一丝意外。可那惊讶只停了一瞬，便化作一种面对命运的释然。
“纵使他们不怪罪，” 他说， “我又岂能问心无愧？”
一切都在意料之中。但船头的青年显然不满意这个答案。
“项王，恕臣直言。” 他说， “大王自万军之中冒死杀至此处，求的，不就是一线生机么？如今船在眼前，江东在对岸。为何偏偏不肯上船？”
en: Xiang Yu turned toward the ferry. Surprise flickered in his eyes when he saw that the voice belonged to a young woman. It lasted only an instant, then gave way to the serenity of a man who had accepted his fate.
“Even if they do not blame me,” he said, “how could I be without shame before my own heart?”
Everything had unfolded as expected. But the young man at the bow was plainly dissatisfied with the answer.

“King Xiang, forgive my bluntness.” he said. “Your Majesty fought through an entire army to reach this place. Was it not for one last chance to live? The boat is before you; Jiangdong lies across the river. Why refuse to board now?”

zh: 项羽没有立刻回答。
他望向浓雾中那道巨大的身影，片刻后才收回目光，视线掠过船头的青年，最终落在从乌篷里探出半个身子的月牙儿身上。他的重瞳里没有怒意，只有一种近乎冰冷的清明。
en: Xiang Yu did not answer at once.

He looked toward the immense shape in the fog. Only after a moment did he turn away. His gaze passed over the young man at the bow and came to rest on Mahina, half-emerged from beneath the canopy. There was no anger in his double pupils, only an almost glacial clarity.

zh: “吾自阴陵迷道，” 他缓缓道， “田父绐我，陷于大泽。大雾锁江，芦苇没人，断断续续，不辨南北，连走到了乌江哪一段，亦不自知。”
“可你，却似早知我今日必至，驾着这江上唯一一条渡船，正正候在我脚下这片滩头。”
“你来告诉我，这是为何？”
青年语塞了。他张了张口，一个字也答不出来。
en: “I lost my way at Yinling,” he said slowly. “A farmer deceived me and led me into the great marsh. Fog sealed the river; reeds rose over a man’s head. I wandered on, unable to tell north from south. I do not even know upon which reach of the Wujiang I now stand.”
“Yet you appear to have known that I would come today. You brought the only ferry on this river and waited upon the very shoal at my feet.”
“Tell me—why?”
The young man was struck speechless. His mouth opened, but not a word came out.

zh: 项羽看着他，忽然大笑出声。
“籍，亦非愚钝之人。” 他道， “这乌江之上，何来的亭长？又何来的渡船？”
“天意要亡我。尔等云中之人，又何意来渡我?”
en: Xiang Yu looked at him and suddenly burst into laughter.
“I, Ji, am no fool.” he said. “What pavilion chief could there be upon the Wujiang? What ferry could there be?”
“Heaven wills my death. And you Cloud Dwellers—what purpose brings you here to ferry me across?”

zh: 雾从江面上滚过。无人答话。从走出芦苇荡、看见这条船的那一刻起，他就全知道了。
en: Fog rolled over the river. No one answered. From the moment he had stepped out of the reeds and seen the boat, he had understood everything.

zh: 隆隆的马蹄声由远及近。芦苇荡外影影绰绰，已经望得见骑兵的影子，汉军赤色的战旗在雾中时隐时现。
有人在远处高声喊着，声音被风撕得断断续续：
“汉王有令——得项羽头者，赏千金，邑万户——！”
en: The thunder of hooves drew nearer. Beyond the reeds, cavalry shadows had begun to show; the red battle standards of the Han army appeared and vanished in the mist.
Someone shouted in the distance, the wind tearing the words to pieces:
“By decree of the King of Han—whoever takes Xiang Yu’s head shall receive a thousand pieces of gold and a fief of ten thousand households—!”

zh: 结局到了。这一刻，江边所有人都知道。
en: The end had arrived. Everyone on the riverbank knew it.
